_: The ground's look (land3d.gd, terrain.gd read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). The painted look (art-direction/concept-town-repaint.png; Foundation and Tiny Glade's soft painted ground): layers: Terrain3D's ground layers, each a painting of the look audit's painted ground (assets/ground/painted_v2, docs/art/ground/sheet.jpg; packed by tools/pack_painted_ground.gd into assets/ground/terrain3d), its scale (texture repeats per game unit: the paintings are about 4 m a tile, 2 a unit) and, if ever needed, a tint (multiplies it; the paint is final, none now); a wider beach, no surf at the shore. beach.top: how far above the waterline the shore's ground runs, ramping in to the water (game units; 0.07: a soft blend, WC3's shores through dirt; at 0.015 in rock it drew a hard yellow stroke round every coast, g30), beach.layer the ground it is. beach.snow: [below, from] heights (game units) between which winter's snow comes in over the shore: none on the tide-washed beach below the first, whole from the second (g10 crossing: the beach white as snow). roads: a grass verge either side of each track (verge: its width as a share of the road's; vergeTint: its colour and strength, near the grass's own so it blends, not a yellow band); tint: every road's, street's and track's earth, a multiply on the painted road (assets/ground/painted_v2/dirt_road.png; 1: as painted); kingsShade: the King's road that much darker; edge: how a track frays into the grass (feather: the soft edge's width as a share of the road's; wander: how far its verges wander in and out; crown: how solid the grassy strip down the middle stays, 1 none; ruts: how dark the two wheel ruts; ends: how far each stretch's ends fray out, as a share of a tile, so the stretches of a street overlap softly instead of ending square, batch 6 (c)). wear (wear.gd): paths worn where people walk (only where they moved at least walkMin units since the last stamp: standing people wear no pads); on, how much a step wears (0..1), how much grows back each upload, how often people are stamped and the wear uploaded (seconds), the bare earth's colour. macro: Terrain3D's broad colour patches over every layer (research #3, the big low-frequency hue tint): two colours (a lush green, a sun-dried yellow), scale the patches' noise (lower is broader; Terrain3D noise1_scale), slope how much slopes take it; set whether the ground is painted or not. painting: which of the painted set's textures the layer draws (the look audit's painted ground, assets/ground/painted_v2; packed by tools/pack_painted_ground.gd into assets/ground/terrain3d); every layer takes one (tools/ground_check.gd fails a layer that doesn't); lift: how far the painting is washed toward white (the pack has no snow: the snow is its palest stone, lifted). winter.snow: the colour winter's snow lies in, over the land, the roofs (snow.gdshader) and the leaves (snow_leaf.gdshader) alike (g24 raid: roofs at 0.9 and the land at 0.74 blew out near white; g25: 0.66-0.79 read as grey mud, now 0.74-0.86, a soft blue-white between); winter.paint: how much of the painted ground (roads, squares, fields, worn paths: terrain.gd paint) the snow hides at full cover, so tracks show as trodden lines, never orange through it (g25 raid) (land3d.gd snow_col; was 0.84, 0.86, 0.91: the light pass found the square's blown whites were mostly snow, so about 0.88 of it, its blue cast kept). mesh: Terrain3D's rings of land round the lens (size: vertices across the finest ring, each further ring twice as coarse; lods: how many rings). Its default 48 drew the mid zoom's ground from points 2 units apart, sinking a lake's low shore under the water's surface (the grey smear, fields seen lying on the lake); 128 keeps half-unit detail out to about 30 units. rivers (rivers.gd): never a square end. mouthUnder: how far under the sea's or a lake's surface a river's mouth sinks (game units); mouthEase: over how many of its last points (half a unit apart) it eases down; taper: over how many points a spring's head or a river running into another narrows; thin: how narrow, as a share of its width; shallow, deep: the water's colour (the old peaty 0.2/0.26/0.2 read near black from the mid zoom).
_layers: Each layer's painting (painted_v2), its scale (repeats a game unit: lower is larger; the grass 1.0 so the drawn-back view reads no speckle) and calm, applied when tools/pack_painted_ground.gd packs it: contrast (how much of each texel's difference from the painting's mean stays), sat (saturation kept), mult (a colour multiply): WC3's low-contrast tiles (docs/research/terrain-wc3-method.md; g30 landuse, Mac: oversaturated yellow-green speckle). macro a/b: the large soft wash over it, dark and lush green, never yellow.

terrain._: g37 (vs 02-realm: green hills, rock on crests, snow on peaks): Hills grass with stony ground and a little rock (was rock 0.6 over grass 0.5, every hill tile grey rock); Mountains rock over grass 0.6/0.3 (was 1/0.1); Glacier and Tundra no flat snow (was snow 1 and 0.3: tile-shaped white sheets at any height); snow lies only by height (peaks.snow). The ground by Freeciv's terrain (terrain.gd tile_mix; land3d.gd lays the strongest layer over the grass, blended across tile edges): each terrain's weights of the ground layers in land3d.gd's order: grass, dirt (the painted earth), sand, snow, rock, forest, mud, field, dry grass, stony. A river tile (Grassland|river) takes its terrain's. Water tiles are grass here: the beach and the sea floor come from the land's height. patches: a list of patches through the grass, each its own noise: worn earth (Mac, pass 2159: one flat lawn outside the towns; 01-town and 03-army show bare earth and varied ground), drier grass in large soft drifts and darker woodland floor (g33 landuse: one flat green; WC3's large soft variation): layer (its index), most (its weight at a patch's heart, times the tile's grass), from (the noise level where a patch starts: higher, fewer), soft (how far it frays), scale (noise per game unit: higher, smaller patches).
terrain._patches: g38 battle and muster lawns read one flat green: the overlay blend is patch/(grass+patch), so most 0.75 topped out near 0.4 and the height blend mostly kept the grass. Now a lawn is four grounds as WC3 blends them: worn dirt (1), a broad dry-grass wash (8) and a near-scale dry tuft (8 again, scale 0.6), dark floor (5) and rough stony patches (9).

tiers._: terrain.gd _terrace: the hills stepped into shelves with steep faces between (WC3's cliff levels), above from (game units): each step of height a shelf, its last ramp share rising to the next; fading in over over; never by a river. g35: a step every 0.9 drew the hills as nine thin contour stripes; every 2.0 from 2.0 up to 7.0, three bold shelves (WC3's two or three cliff levels). g36: off. Stepping the eroded heightmap drew a cliff contour round every hill at every level, rice terraces across the east; WC3's cliffs are placed by hand, not cut by height, so the hills are AoE2's smooth sun-shaded slopes with rock only where steep (docs/research/terrain-wc3-method.md point 4).

blend._: land3d.gd: Terrain3D's blend_sharpness, how hard one ground gives way to the next (it blends by each layer's painted height; 0.87 snapped the bright snow over with a hard rim, g36). 0.5: soft painted transitions (WC3).

paint._: terrain.gd paint: every painted ground (roads, fields, squares, worn paths) fades where the ground under it turns steep (Godot Decal.normal_fade: 0 never; 0.5 gone on a face steeper than about 60 degrees), so a decal by a bank never streaks down the slope (g38 siege).

auto._: land3d.gd _control_from_land: the auto shader (rock on cliffs, by slope) only where the ground is this steep or bare grass; cliff, the normal's height under which it is a cliff (lower, fewer cliffs).
auto._slope: g38 realm: no rock on any crest, the hills mottled olive: cliff 0.88 (was 0.82, about 35 degrees; now about 28), between g37's gully stripes (0.94) and none; layers.rock.calm contrast 1.0, sat 0.7 (were 0.75, 0.62): the slabs' light and shadow kept, so a crest reads as stone, not grey paint. slope: Terrain3D auto_slope, how soon a slope turns rock (higher: gentler slopes rock; was 1.6, the hills read as grass mounds); high: auto_height_reduction, rock creeping over high ground (0, was 4: g34's realm view had every upland rock from height alone, one cold grey-blue skin with no peak standing out; rock now only where it is steep: crests, tier faces, cliffs; slope 2.0, was 2.6). g37: still grey stripes down every eroded gully: cliff 0.82 (was 0.94, rock from about 20 degrees), slope 1.4 (was 2.0). layers.rock.calm warmed (mult 0.98, 0.94, 0.86, was 0.92, 0.94, 0.98; sat 0.62, was 0.5): 02-realm's mountains are warm brown-grey, not blue.

hosts._: wear.gd _facts: a host in the field wears a camp where it stands (radius camp + camp_per_men x sqrt(men), at most camp_max, game units; step a reading) and a track along the land route it moved by (track: its half-width as a share of the camp's; only moves under track_most units).

gates._: wear.gd _facts: the trodden ground at every town gate: out (game units the worn path runs out), half (its half-width at the gate), spread (how much wider it fans by its end), worn (how much).

roads._: wear.gd _facts: Freeciv's roads wear their verges (width: half-width, game units; worn: how much; floor: the share of it that never grows back; per_reading: links laid each reading).

dual._: land3d.gd: the grass's second, larger scale blended in between near and far (game units from the lens), reduction its size against the first.

peaks._: land3d.gd _control_from_land, terrain.gd _layers_at: snow on the mountains, from snow[0] game units, whole at snow[1] (7.4 to 9.6: only the peaks, soft-edged over 2.2 units; g34: the snow lay as flat white paper patches; 6.2 to 7.8 in 922ecaa2 spread them further). ragged: the snow's edge jittered this much in height by noise of scale (a game unit), so it lies in drifts, not as a shelf's flat sheet with a hard rim (g35). tiers.to: above it the hills stop stepping, so peaks rise whole.

wild._bush_reach: vegetation.gd: bushes drawn out to this from the camera (was reach x 1.5, 36: the middle zoom's open country lost them, WC3's doodads stand at every zoom).
